title: Claude-shaped science starts with tasks that suit today’s AI
friendlyTitle: Use AI for the kind of science it can do well today
summary: Physicist Matthew Schwartz describes building BootLoops, an open-source harness that directs language models toward broad, code-heavy and verifiable scientific problems rather than asking them to imitate an independent scientist. Work with domain experts then helped distinguish technically correct connections from scientifically useful ones.
friendlySummary: A physicist built an open-source system that gives AI broad, code-heavy problems with answers that people can check. Experts then decide whether the results are truly useful.
whyItMatters: The practical lesson reaches beyond research: redesign work around what a model can reliably do, make outputs checkable and keep experts responsible for relevance. That is more useful than forcing AI into a human-shaped role and hoping fluency will cover the mismatch.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI works better when the task fits its strengths. Give it checkable work and keep a person responsible for meaning and quality.
